authority: Evidence floors per docs/REBUILD-SPEC.md Appendix A, carrying OWNER-RULINGS W1/W2 (generic core), W4 (Apple), W5+W8.1 (Galaxy), W6/W8.3 (Bitcoin) and the AB2 mandate additions, plus the etf/basket/theme classes per docs/THEMES-BASKETS-SPEC.md section 4 (the W2.5 vehicle floor; AB12 thematic vehicles; basket tests at the thesis level). Floors are minimums for these subjects, never the ceiling: the evidence stage still derives what THIS question needs. Version 1.1.0 adds the ANCHORLESS registry per docs/ANCHORLESS-SPEC.md sections 2-4 (owner rulings AB13.4 and AB15): the gold and commodity subject SHAPES, the asset_classes anchor sets that decide sufficiency for an asset without earnings, and the anchorless_rating constants that fix the rating bar and its bands in data. Version 1.1.1 adds the `substitute` terms on the single_stock capital-spending floor, carrying owner ruling AB19: a filer that publishes no capital-spending line does not stop the council, but the stand-in must declare itself and be labelled, and this data is what the sufficiency gate enforces it against. Version 1.3.0 carries owner ruling AC1 into the single_stock class: segment revenue, the guided figure beside the delivered one, a peer set, and what management owns are conditional minimums - present, or declared absent with a reason - and how long the chief executive has been in the job and what the published consensus expects are advisory. The third canonical test, rating against own history or peers, keeps its id and its meaning; the runbook now says peers are expected wherever a peer set exists. Version 1.3.1 carries owner ruling AC12.3: `revenue_families` below names, as data rather than as code, the fact families a business frame's revenue line may point at - the whole-business revenue figures, any segment revenue line, and their prior-year pairs - so a seat cannot be shown the mix of the business argued from a number that is not revenue. A derived fact struck from facts in those families counts as one of them; the provenance gate reads this entry and enforces it. Version 1.4.0 carries owner ruling AC15 (P2 and P4), unit U3e: `archetype_measures` below is the rule, as data, that a subject's rating measure follows its business archetype; and `cycle` below carries the one data constant that scales a cycle series' freshness to the class's own price-freshness rule. Version 1.4.1 carries owner ruling AC19, unit U3f: `prose_figure_marks` below holds, as data rather than as code, the tolerances and the exemption list the render-time scanner uses to trace every number in a business frame's prose to a recorded fact - the relative tolerance, the year range, the plain-count ceiling, the ordinal suffixes, the scale words, the percent words, the month words, and the units that count as percent, as fraction, and as a currency scale. A number that traces to no fact is MARKED where the prose is shown and the pack is never refused for it. Version 1.5.0 carries owner ruling AC4, unit U4(a): `price_series` below holds the rules a captured daily price series is checked against - the bar count, the longest gap, the freshness of the last bar, and the exchange-holiday lists as data - and `benchmarks` holds the benchmark per asset class (spec U4.2): US equity against SPY, a non-US listing against the broad-index ETF of its primary listing named for the sitting, a coin, bullion and a commodity against nothing (absolute), a basket or theme against its members' class benchmark, and a per-sitting override in the capture that wins over all of it. Version 1.6.0 carries owner rulings AC28 and AC30, unit FI-ARCHETYPE: the archetype table gains a fifth archetype, the financial institution, in six sub-types each carrying its own measure; `fi_families` names the capital and cost-of-risk fact families as data; `archetype_floors` holds the floors merged on top of the single_stock class for each sub-type, with the one lift that makes distributable capital, not capital spending, answer the free-cash test for a bank, an insurer, a reinsurer or a financial holding; and the exited-business ban reaches the profits and client money of a financial institution. Version 1.7.0 carries owner ruling AC4, unit U4(b): a single stock gains two conditional floors - insiders' dealings over the last twelve months (`insider_flow_`) and the company's own buying of its shares (`buyback_`), the market-structure seat's second examination - each present, or declared absent by design with the prefix itself as the gap's class; the prefix is `insider_flow_`, not a bare `insider_`, so what management owns cannot stand in for what insiders did.

entry_kinds.id: the exact fact id must be present in tier1
entry_kinds.one_of: at least one of the listed fact ids must be present in tier1
entry_kinds.prefix: at least one tier1 fact id starting with the prefix must be present
entry_kinds.pairs: where the first id of a pair is present in tier1, the second must be too
entry_kinds.prefix_pairs: a family that only means anything in pairs: at least one tier1 fact id starting with `prefix` must be present, and every one of them must carry its companion - the same id with `companion_prefix` in place of `prefix`. What management guided for a quarter says nothing on its own; beside what it delivered it says whether management hits its own numbers
entry_kinds.parallel_prefixes: every listed prefix must be present in tier1 AND the suffixes after the prefixes must be the SAME SET across all of them - a repeated structure (one row per cycle, one row per venue) is complete or it is not there; an optional min_members says how many members the structure needs before it is a structure at all
entry_kinds.requires_arithmetic: the fact IS built from other facts in the pack, so it must declare its arithmetic and the gate recomputes it - a claimed difference is asserted, not shown. The companion `arithmetic` names the operation and the operand fact ids IN ORDER, because a capture that adds where the anchor subtracts would otherwise have its own wrong sum faithfully verified
entry_kinds.substitute: AB19 as AB20 reshapes it, capital spending ONLY: where the capture declares the named gap class as absent by design, the fact is a stand-in for a line the filer does not publish, and the ruling's machine-knowable terms bind - both years TAGGED as ceilings naming the SAME published line, struck by the same operation over the same number of operands, every operand of both a reading the capture actually carries, and each named free-cash-flow fact BOTH struck against its own year's ceiling AND tagged as a floor. The declaration is the capture's own bound tag, never words hunted out of a source sentence. Undeclared, the entry behaves as its level alone says - and a stand-in tag on the fact with no declared gap is itself refused, because AB19 requires the gap row alongside
entry_kinds.levels: required = missing refuses; conditional = missing refuses unless a gap is declared with the stated reason; advisory = recorded, never refuses

revenue_families.why: AC12.3 (owner, 2026-09-08): a revenue line in the business frame may point ONLY at revenue. Before this rule a line could cite any fact the pack carried - the last price included - and the case file printed that id under the heading 'Facts that carry it', so a seat could argue the mix of the business from a number that is not revenue. Named here as DATA so the families can be widened by a ruling without touching code. A member of a basket or a theme carries the same ids under its own '__<ticker>' suffix; the gate strips that suffix before it reads this list.
revenue_families.derived: a derived fact counts as revenue where every operand it is struck from is itself revenue by this list, however many steps down - the share of the period a line carries is exactly such a fact

asset_classes.authority: ANCHORLESS-SPEC sections 2 and 4 (owner rulings AB13.4 and AB15): the asset class decides the sufficiency anchor set and the rating basis, and nothing else. The class lists below are the owner's own confirmed lists, including the PBoC enhancement he added to gold's central-bank anchor. Later classes are ADDITIONS to this data, never code.

common_anchorless.note: Applied to EVERY anchorless class on top of its own list: the anchors the commissioned brief calls class-generic (the dated event calendar and five-year realized volatility; the price with its freshness rule sits in each class's own list, because the ruled ceiling differs by class) plus the cash rate, because ANCHORLESS-SPEC section 3 makes cash and the five-year volatility the two inputs of the rating bar itself. A pack that cannot answer the bar cannot earn a rating, which is the failure this unit exists to fix.

crypto.reading_rule: Every cohort figure here is read BESIDE the fund flows. Roughly 1.3 million coins now sit inside exchange-traded funds, custodied overwhelmingly by one firm, and a coin moving into fund custody resets its age to day one. In a heavy-creation period the coin-age split and the cost bases partly measure custody plumbing rather than investor behaviour - and the record says so rather than silently trusting them.

omitted.nupl: Net unrealised profit/loss is exactly one minus the reciprocal of MVRV - a rearrangement of a metric already required. Requiring both would let one fact vote twice.
omitted.whale_and_address_cohorts: An address is not a person. Fund custody compresses millions of owners into a handful of very large addresses, so 'whales are accumulating' now frequently means 'a fund had a creation'. The most corrupted family after the ETFs arrived, and the most likely to produce a confident wrong answer.
omitted.thermocap_stock_to_flow_pi_cycle: No mechanism. Thermocap divides by a quantity that only ever grows, so it is never actionable at a decision horizon; stock-to-flow was falsified in public; Pi-cycle and rainbow charts are curve-fits to three prior cycles.
omitted.active_addresses_and_nvt: Both assume on-chain transaction activity proxies economic activity. Most trading is now off-chain or inside fund wrappers, so it no longer does.

seat_emphasis.advisor_bear: the on-chain valuation floor: the realized price, the two cost bases of recent and patient owners, and what actually breaks on the way down to each of them.
seat_emphasis.advisor_bull: the macro and the dated calendar: the risk-free rate, the policy and protocol dates in play, and what the calendar could deliver inside the horizon.
seat_emphasis.advisor_base_rate: the cycle history WITH ITS DURATIONS: prior peaks, troughs, depths and the months each recovery took - how far, and how long.
seat_emphasis.advisor_market_structure: the flows and the positioning: spot-ETF flows and their cumulative series, the basis or funding rate, open interest, and the patient-owner supply change read beside the flows.
seat_emphasis.advisor_risk: the asset's own risk: realized volatility over five years, the drawdown shape the cycle history records, the hash rate and difficulty as the production system's health, and forced miner supply.

gold.note: ANCHORLESS-SPEC 4.B, confirmed by the owner at freeze with his PBoC enhancement (AB15), grounded in the commissioned gold/commodity brief of 2026-09-01. Gold is a MONETARY asset, not a commodity: essentially every ounce ever mined still exists and annual mine supply is about 1.5 per cent of that stock, so nothing on the supply side moves the price. The anchors answer one question - who is buying, why, and what would make them stop.

gold.reading_rule: Official-sector buying is a SLOW series: it is published quarterly and runs two to five months behind. Its as-of date is rendered beside it at every sitting, so its age is read rather than assumed - a stale figure honestly dated is evidence; a stale figure read as current is not.

omitted.mining_cost_floor: Miners' all-in costs run near 39 per cent of the gold price. A floor 60 per cent below the market is not a floor - it is a statement about mining profits. It becomes relevant only when a MINING COMPANY is the subject, which is a different asset class.
omitted.lease_and_forward_rates: No free public benchmark exists: the London forward rate was discontinued in January 2015 and rates are now private dealer quotes.
omitted.ratio_of_anchor_metrics: Gold-to-equities and gold-to-inflation are quotients of figures the council already holds. Never anchor on the division of two anchors - it creates a way for a sitting to be refused over arithmetic.

seat_emphasis.advisor_bear: the valuation check: the inflation-adjusted price against its own long history, and what has ended prior episodes at comparable levels.
seat_emphasis.advisor_bull: the official-sector bid: central-bank buying with its as-of date, the PBoC's reported figure beside the market's estimate of its true buying, and whether the bull case needs real yields to fall or can name the buyer paying up regardless.
seat_emphasis.advisor_base_rate: the outside view on real yields: what the five- and ten-year inflation-protected yields pay, what the textbook relationship says should follow, and how often it has actually proved true.
seat_emphasis.advisor_market_structure: who is setting the price now: fund holdings and monthly flows, speculative futures positioning, and the broad dollar as the denominator under the whole move.
seat_emphasis.advisor_risk: the asset's own risk: five-year realized volatility, the crowding in speculative positioning, and how much of the move would unwind if the fast money left.

commodity.note: ANCHORLESS-SPEC 4.C, the TEMPLATE for any standalone commodity, confirmed by the owner at freeze (AB15). A commodity is dug up, consumed and stored, so it genuinely runs short and long, and the market says so through inventories and the shape of the forward curve. It cannot be owned without cost or contract, so the council analyses it through the instrument it would actually buy (the owner's ruled product-conditional rule, W2.7).

commodity.capture_fragility: RECORDED, not solved: the only free London metals price and inventory feed is a scraped third-party mirror with no service guarantee - a single point of failure sitting under a required anchor. A sitting that must use it carries a stated confidence note on those facts, per the primary-or-discounted rule. A fallback path is REGISTERED, not built (ANCHORLESS-SPEC section 4.C).

omitted.demand_narratives: Grid spending, property and vehicle demand are the fashionable items and exactly what to leave out. In a storable commodity, demand reveals itself in inventories and in the curve, both already required; requiring the story on top double-counts it and gives a sitting a plumbing reason to fail while adding no measurement the price has not already made.
omitted.separate_storage_cost_inputs: The forward curve already prices storage and financing. Requiring separate inputs is arithmetic the market has done for us, and would be wrong more often than the curve.

seat_emphasis.advisor_bear: the loose case: inventories venue by venue, what the curve says about surplus, and what the price would be without the policy component in it.
seat_emphasis.advisor_bull: the tight case: the carry read off the curve, the inventory trend, and the dated calendar events that could tighten the market inside the horizon.
seat_emphasis.advisor_base_rate: the outside view: what has happened to comparable products at comparable inventory levels and comparable curve shapes.
seat_emphasis.advisor_market_structure: the venue structure: the executable price with its venue and month, the cross-venue gap and how much of it is policy rather than material, and open interest at the horizon.
seat_emphasis.advisor_risk: the asset's own risk: five-year realized volatility, the tradable horizon against the thesis's own horizon, and the roll requirement the trade would carry.

copper.note: The first registry entry (ANCHORLESS-SPEC section 8: further products return to the owner when charged). Copper's conditional item is the three-venue inventory split, and the relocation trap it guards against.

anchors.likely_source: the London venue's published warehouse stocks, dated - free only through a scraped mirror today, so carry the confidence note
anchors.why: ANCHORLESS-SPEC 4.C.4 for copper: the London stock, one of the three that must be read together

anchors.likely_source: the New York venue's published warehouse stocks, dated
anchors.why: ANCHORLESS-SPEC 4.C.4 for copper: the New York stock. During the tariff scramble metal moved from London warehouses to New York ones while total inventory barely changed

anchors.likely_source: the Shanghai venue's published warehouse stocks, dated
anchors.why: ANCHORLESS-SPEC 4.C.4 for copper: the Shanghai stock - without it the split is two thirds of a picture

bar_inputs.note: The three frozen facts the chairman's ladder is allowed to name. They are the class anchors themselves, named here in ONE place so the engine binds the ladder to the facts it claims rather than to any figure carried in the same unit: a funding rate is a percentage too, and a bar built on it instead of the bill rate rates a losing ladder hold (audit finding ANCHORLESS-B r1-4).

anchorless_rating.authority: ANCHORLESS-SPEC section 3 (owner rulings AB13.1-.3). The scaling rule and the band arithmetic are the builder's to fix IN DATA; every constant here is stated in the verdict and printed on the page, and the machine - never a seat - computes the arithmetic from them.
anchorless_rating.reading: The bar is CASH plus a premium scaled to the asset's own five-year realized volatility. Read it as a required reward for risk: bar_volatility_multiple is the minimum extra return per unit of the asset's own volatility that the council demands before it will call anything a buy. The bands above it are measured in the same volatility units, so one scaling step means the same thing everywhere.
bands: sell: the expected annualised result is below cash - the asset is expected to lose against a Treasury bill
hold: the expected annualised result clears cash but does not clear the bar decisively - it beats cash without paying for the risk taken
buy: the expected annualised result clears the bar by at least buy_excess_multiple times the asset's own five-year volatility
strong_buy: it clears the bar by at least strong_buy_excess_multiple times that volatility
monitor: the chairman judged the ladder too uncertain to aggregate, and said why - a watch-state, never a fifth opinion
anchorless_rating.sensitivity: ALWAYS printed (AB13.2): the probability at which the rating flips to the next rating down, and the bar recomputed one scaling step above and one below.

correction_reaudit.authority: Owner ruling AC15 (P8), unit U3d. A user correction that only NARROWS a claim needs no outside re-audit; a REBUILDING correction - one that changes what the seats reason from - requires a delta re-audit before the sufficiency gate passes. A correction is rebuilding when the corrected fact, or any figure struck from it, is one the business frame's reading rests on (cited in any section named below) or a headline pair (revenue, net income or operating cash flow against its prior-year pair). It narrows otherwise. A correction that brought a new fact or a new derived chain into the pack would also rebuild, but the correction command sets an existing, non-derived fact's value only and can produce neither. This list is DATA so a ruling can widen or narrow it without a code change - the discipline the revenue families already live under (owner ruling AC12.3).

period_basis.authority: Owner ruling AC15 (P3), unit U3d. An average must not be published as an annual figure. A derived fact that PRESENTS itself as an annual, per-year or run-rate figure - its id or label carries one of the signal words below - must declare which period it covers, and one that declares a multi-year or lifetime average basis while calling itself annual is refused: that is the conflation the owner flagged, a multi-decade average run rate read as the first twelve months' billing. The signal words and the average bases are DATA so a ruling can widen them without a code change. The set of legal bases is the capture contract's own period_basis enum; a fact struck by dividing a total by a term declares its basis by naming itself for what it is, which is what makes it, or keeps it from being, presented as annual.

archetype_measures.authority: Owner ruling AC15 (P2), unit U3e. The third canonical test declares the subject's ARCHETYPE - what kind of business it is - and the rating MEASURE that archetype calls for. This table is that rule as DATA, so a ruling can widen it without a code change - the discipline the revenue families and the correction re-audit rules already live under. The sufficiency gate enforces it for a single name only, and it never reads whether the declared archetype is TRUE (no machine can read a filing); it checks only that the measure matches the archetype, that the measure's numerator is present for the subject, and that the rating is computable for every peer - the peer numerator AND each denominator metric the rating_vs_history_or_peers row names in 'peer_denominator_metrics', all under the peer_<metric>__<ticker> convention - or the peer half is the declared 'peer_' gap (architect ruling 2026-09-20: a ratio is not computable from its numerator alone, so requiring only the peer numerator was too weak - a peer that carries enterprise value but no contracted capacity cannot be set beside the subject on enterprise value per contracted megawatt). The peer-side denominator ids differ by subject, so the capturer names them on the row rather than this table fixing them; for a profitable_operator the denominator is the earnings comparator (the price/earnings figure). The subject's own denominators are the frame's decisive metrics, whose ids differ by subject and so are not named here. Architect ruling 2026-09-20 (unit U3e, closing round-1 findings r1-1 and r1-3): 'computable' means BOTH halves of the ratio on BOTH sides, so each measure carries a 'denominators_required' count as DATA, and the rating_vs_history_or_peers row names that many 'subject_denominator_facts' (tier-1 fact ids) beside that many 'peer_denominator_metrics' (metric names). The sufficiency gate refuses a count that does not match the measure's, and holds each named subject denominator to the same bar as the numerator - a tier-1 reading, fresh, and a finite number; the peer half (its metric count and the per-peer denominators) is required only when no 'peer_' gap is declared. The capturer still names the facts; this table fixes only how many the measure needs.

profitable_operator.note: A business earning money, rated on earnings against its own history and its peers. The market value is the always-present anchor of an earnings multiple; the earnings side is the first canonical test's own facts (profit_growth), already required. denominators_required is 1: the earnings comparator (the price/earnings figure) is the one denominator the market value is divided by, named on the row's subject_denominator_facts for the subject and peer_denominator_metrics for the peers.

ramping_infrastructure_builder.note: A business whose revenue has not arrived yet, rated on enterprise value per unit of contracted capacity and contracted revenue per unit - the TeraWulf finding. The contracted-capacity and rent-per-unit denominators are the frame's decisive metrics; their ids differ by subject. denominators_required is 2: both the contracted capacity and the contracted revenue per unit are named on the row's subject_denominator_facts for the subject and peer_denominator_metrics for the peers.

stabilised_lessor.note: A business earning steady rent on built-out capacity, rated on enterprise value to operating income. Operating income is the denominator, the frame's own decisive metric. denominators_required is 1: operating income is the one denominator enterprise value is divided by, named on the row's subject_denominator_facts for the subject and peer_denominator_metrics for the peers.

no_earnings_asset.note: An asset with no earnings - it keeps the AB13/AB15 anchorless ladder untouched, and this archetype is legal only for an anchorless subject. denominators_required is 0: the ladder is not a ratio and names no denominators; the subject_denominator_facts and peer_denominator_metrics checks do not run for an anchorless archetype.

financial_institution.note: Owner rulings AC28 and AC30 (unit FI-ARCHETYPE; research brief 2026-09-23). A business whose balance sheet is its product, or whose product is the stewardship of clients' capital: rated on the return it earns on the capital it is required to hold (a manager: the client capital entrusted to it) against the price the market pays for that capital. One archetype, six sub-types; the frame's fi_subtype selects the row below, and every key of that row is read exactly as a top-level archetype row is read. The numerator is the whole economic market value of the COMMON equity - every participating class and exchangeable unit, never the preferred - and a balance-sheet or manager sub-type divides it by TWO amounts, the capital base and the trailing earnings on it, so price-to-capital, price-to-earnings and the return on capital are struck from the same three facts for the subject and every peer. A financial holding divides by ONE, its net asset value, struck as a derived chain the nav_bridge declares. denominator_roles names what each subject denominator IS, in the order the rating row lists them; denominator_ids names, per role in the same order, the fact ids that role may be (architect ruling closing P-FIa-1, from the brief's per-sub-type rows), checked on the subject's denominators and the peers' denominator metrics alike - the continuing business's figure (fi_exited_business) carries the same id with its suffix.

bank.note: A deposit-funded lender, trader or custodian under a prudential capital rule. Denominators: tangible common equity at the latest quarter end, and net income applicable to common over the trailing four quarters (suggested ids tangible_common_equity, net_income_to_common_ttm; the capturer names them on the row).

insurer.note: A life, P&C or composite insurer. Denominators: the equity base the company's own operating return on equity divides by, and operating (core) net income attributable over the trailing four quarters (suggested ids equity_for_operating_roe, operating_earnings_ttm). Each peer on its own definition, the definition named in not_comparable_on.

reinsurer.note: A reinsurer. Denominators: shareholders' equity (tangible book for a US GAAP reporter) and net income attributable over the trailing four quarters (suggested ids equity_for_roe, net_income_ttm). A normal catastrophe year is shown by the large-loss budget/actual pair, never by a normalised figure.

traditional_asset_manager.note: A capital-light manager of long-only and index client assets. Denominators: assets under management at the latest quarter end, and as-adjusted net income over the trailing four quarters (suggested ids aum_period_end, adjusted_net_income_ttm).

alternative_asset_manager.note: A private-markets manager. The market value is struck on the economic share count including exchangeable units. Denominators: fee-earning assets at the latest quarter end, and fee-related earnings over the trailing four quarters (suggested ids fee_earning_aum_period_end, fre_ttm).

financial_holding.note: A holding company whose assets are mostly financial institutions. The one denominator is nav_total, a DERIVED chain: each listed stake at its market value, each unlisted holding at the company's reported value, plus holding-company cash less holding-company debt and preferred. The frame's nav_bridge names the parts; the discount's own history is the conditional nav_published_hist_/price_hist_ structure. The owned companies are not re-rated in the same sitting (AC30(3)).

forbidden_on_model_transition.why: Owner ruling AC15 (P2): rating a business that is CHANGING its model on trailing revenue drawn from the business it is exiting is explicitly forbidden - the WULF finding, where the headline revenue is mostly the segment being closed. Where the frame's what_is_changing.kind is 'model_transition' and the rating row rests on any fact id named here, the sufficiency gate refuses. Named as DATA so a ruling can widen the list without a code change: revenue_q and its prior-year pair are the whole-business trailing revenue; an EV-to-revenue multiple a capture strikes for the exited business is added here by id. Owner ruling AC28 (unit FI-ARCHETYPE) adds the revenue ids of a financial institution - net revenue, insurance revenue, gross written premiums and base fees, each with its prior-year pair - within the same meaning.

fi_exited_business.why: Owner ruling AC30(4) (G4): for a financial institution the exited-business ban reaches profits and client money, not only revenue. On a model_transition FI, every subject denominator whose role is named below must be the CONTINUING business's figure, its id ending in the suffix below - a derived fact may strike it from the whole less the part being sold or run off, arithmetic shown.

cycle.why: Owner ruling AC15 (P4), unit U3e. A single name whose thesis rests on an identifiable capital or commodity cycle carries three to five dated series for it, or declares the gap. Each series' as-of freshness is judged against the subject class's own price-freshness rule times the multiple below - a data constant - so a cycle series is measured against a rule scaled from the price the sitting turns on, never a number invented on its own.

fi_families.why: Owner rulings AC28 and AC30, on the model of AC12.3's revenue_families: the fact families the frame's fi_capital and fi_risk_cost may point at, named as DATA so a capital line cannot cite a fact that is not capital and a risk-cost line cannot cite a fact that is not a cost of risk.

risk_cost_kinds.why: Architect ruling closing P-FIa-2 (brief section D): the risk-cost family split by the kind fi_risk_cost declares - a bank's cost of risk is a credit line, an insurer's or reinsurer's an underwriting line - so a line of one kind cannot cite the other kind's fact. Together the kinds cover risk_cost_ids and risk_cost_prefixes exactly.

financial_institution.why: Owner rulings AC28 and AC30. Floors merged ON TOP of the single_stock class floors for a single name whose frame declares archetype financial_institution: the all_subtypes list, then the list for its fi_subtype. Levels as entry_kinds defines them.

free_cash_flow_test_words: the second canonical test, for a bank, insurer, reinsurer or financial holding - how much capital the firm can pay out and still stay above its regulator's minimum

the capital section of the latest results: the capital ratio beside its requirement and management's buffer, earnings retained, dividends and buybacks paid - a distributable_capital_ fact, its arithmetic declared where it is derived
lifts.why: Owner ruling AC30(1) (G1): a bank's or insurer's operating cash flow minus capital spending is noise, so for these sub-types the free-cash test is answered by distributable capital - the earnings left after holding the capital the requirement and growth absorb - and the capital-spending floor is lifted. The test's wording for every other subject is unchanged.

prose_figure_marks.why: Owner ruling AC19, unit U3f. The render-time scanner (council/evidence/trace.py) traces every number written into a business frame's prose to a recorded fact of the pack, allowing for rounding and for a change of scale or unit wording; a number that traces to nothing is MARKED where the prose is shown and the pack is NEVER refused for it. Every tolerance and every exemption the scanner uses lives here as data, not as a constant in the code (AC19(4)).
prose_figure_marks.relative_tolerance_note: The fallback match when the prose number and a fact value do not agree to the prose's own significant figures: they still match when they are within this fraction of each other.
prose_figure_marks.year_note: A four-digit integer in this range, standing on its own, is a year and is never marked.
prose_figure_marks.day_note: A plain integer in this range sitting directly beside a month word is the day of a written date and is never marked, with one exception: a day written AFTER its month ('September 30') is only a date's day when nothing that could be its unit follows it (see date_day_closers) - a following unit word ('September 30 MW') makes it a measured figure that is still marked (architect ruling closing register item P-U3f-2, audit UPGRADE2-U3f r3-1). A percent, currency or scaled figure that merely follows a month name is a figure of the prose and is still marked; a month-year is caught by the year rule (audit UPGRADE2-U3f r2-2).
prose_figure_marks.plain_count_note: A plain integer from 0 to this ceiling, with no currency sign, percent or scale, is a count and is never marked.
prose_figure_marks.date_day_closers_note: For a day written AFTER its month ('September 30'), the day is a written date's day only when the next non-space character after it (and any ordinal suffix) is the end of the text, one of these closers, or the first digit of a four-digit year. Any other following word makes the number a measured figure that is still marked (architect ruling closing register item P-U3f-2, audit UPGRADE2-U3f r3-1). The day-before-month order ('30 September') is unaffected: the month word itself follows the number.
prose_figure_marks.scale_words_note: The power of ten a scale word or letter written directly after a number multiplies it by. Read case-sensitively for the single letters (M is millions) and case-insensitively for the words.
prose_figure_marks.percent_words_note: Words after a number that make it a percentage (the percent SIGN and the two words 'per cent' are read by the scanner directly). A percentage matches a percent-unit or fraction-unit fact, never a plain one.
prose_figure_marks.month_words_note: A plain day-of-month integer (see day_min/day_max) sitting directly beside one of these is the day of a written date and is never marked; the year of a month-year is caught by the year rule. For the day-after-month order ('September 30') a following unit word lifts the exemption - see date_day_closers_note.
prose_figure_marks.currency_scale_units_note: A recorded fact whose unit states a currency scale is read in base units by this power of ten before it is compared to a prose number; a unit not listed here (USD, USD_per_share, MW, years, x) is read at its face value.

price_series.authority: Owner ruling AC4; spec U4.1 (unit U4(a)). The capture may carry the subject's daily closes (price_series) and its ruled benchmark's (benchmark_series); the provenance gate refuses a series that contradicts itself, in plain words, against these numbers. They are data so a ruling can move them without a code change.
price_series.min_bars_note: The subject's series carries at least this many daily bars (about two trading years), or declares its gap - a recent listing has no longer history. A benchmark series follows the same rule and must also span the subject's window.
price_series.max_gap_note: No two consecutive bars may lie more than this many calendar days apart, not counting the days the series' exchange calendar below declares a holiday. A normal weekend is three days; a long weekend four.
price_series.max_staleness_note: The last bar lies at most this many exchange days before the capture's date. An exchange day is a weekday the series' calendar trades (its trading_weekdays, ISO numbering, Monday 1 to Sunday 7) that the calendar does not declare a holiday; on the all-days calendar every calendar day counts. A series naming a calendar the floors do not define refuses.
price_series.calendars_by_asset_class_note: The calendars an UNLISTED subject's price series may name, by its asset class (architect ruling closing P-U4a1-5): a spot coin trades every day. A subject with a listing is bound by calendars_by_listing instead, whatever its shape. An unlisted subject whose class is not listed here (bullion, a contract with no listing recorded) has no calendar defined and its price series refuses until one is added here, as data. The benchmark series is bound by its benchmark's listing through calendars_by_listing (architect ruling closing P-U4a1-8).
price_series.calendars_by_listing_note: The calendar a LISTED subject's price series must name, by its listing (architect ruling closing P-U4a1-5): a stock, a fund, or a basket or theme whose members list, trades on its exchange's calendar whatever it holds - a US-listed fund holding coins trades on the US calendar. Matched ignoring case and extra spaces, whole name only. A listing not named here refuses: add the exchange and its calendar (with the calendar's holidays below) as data before the first sitting that carries such a series.

CRYPTO_24_7.name: All days - a market that trades every calendar day (crypto)
CRYPTO_24_7.note: Every calendar day is a trading day and none is a holiday, so the gap rule and freshness both count calendar days.

XNYS.name: US equity markets (New York Stock Exchange and Nasdaq) - full-day closures
XNYS.note: Full-day market closures, 2023 to 2027, from the exchanges' published holiday calendars, including the national day of mourning on 2025-01-09. Early closes are trading days and are not listed. Extend this list, as data, before a series runs past its last year.

benchmarks.authority: Owner ruling AC4; spec U4.2 (unit U4(a)). The benchmark a price series is judged against, by asset class. The scoring defaults in council/floors/scoring-rules.json name the same SPY for US equity (AC7).

equity.non_us_note: A listing that is not in us_listings below has no default: the capture names the primary listing's broad-index ETF in its top-level benchmark block for the sitting, or the gate refuses a price series carried without one.

benchmarks.absolute_note: A null class benchmark means the subject is judged on its own return (absolute): a coin, bullion and a commodity carry no benchmark series.
benchmarks.collective_note: A basket or theme takes the class benchmark of its members: SPY when every named member lists in the US, otherwise named for the sitting. A fund is read by its own listing.
benchmarks.override_note: A per-sitting override in the capture's top-level benchmark block wins over every default here, including a null ticker that rules the sitting absolute; it states why in its own words, and names the benchmark's listing so its series is judged on that exchange's calendar (architect ruling closing P-U4a1-8).
benchmarks.us_listings_note: Matched against the subject's listing ignoring case and extra spaces, whole name only - 'Nasdaq Stockholm' is not a US listing.
